questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code protects the pending adjustments while they are being read? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
close_period() computes the per-employee totals after leaving the with-block. Why is that safe?
choices: The GIL makes iterating any dict safe in Python
The dict was swapped out under the lock, so no other thread holds a reference to it and add() now writes to a new dict
_net() is a pure function, so it never needs synchronization
The _closed flag prevents any thread from reading the dict

questions.prompt: add() is called concurrently with close_period(). Which statement is correct about each adjustment?
choices: It may be added to the old dict after the swap and silently lost
It is always rejected once close_period() has started
It is always included, because add() waits for the totals to be computed
It is either included in the closed period's totals or rejected with PeriodClosedError

questions.prompt: Two operators click 'Run payroll' at the same instant. What is the outcome?
choices: The first call closes the period and pays; the second logs a warning and returns 0
Both calls pay half of each employee's net amount
The second call blocks until the first finishes, then pays again
